**Jan-Krzysztof Duda** (Polish: [[ˈjan ˌkʂɨʂtɔf ˈduda]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Polish "Help:IPA/Polish") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:LL-Q809_(pol)-Ptjackyll-Jan-Krzysztof_Duda.wav "File:LL-Q809 (pol)-Ptjackyll-Jan-Krzysztof Duda.wav"); born 26 April 1998) is a Polish [chess grandmaster](/wiki/Grandmaster_(chess) "Grandmaster (chess)"). A [prodigy](/wiki/Chess_prodigy "Chess prodigy"), he achieved the grandmaster title in 2013 at the age of 15 years and 21 days. As of December 2025,[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jan-Krzysztof_Duda&action=edit) he is ranked No. 1 in Poland and No. 21 in the [world](/wiki/FIDE_world_rankings "FIDE world rankings"). His personal best  [rating](/wiki/Elo_rating_system "Elo rating system") of 2760 makes him the highest ranked Polish player of all time.

Duda won the [Polish Championship](/wiki/Polish_Chess_Championship "Polish Chess Championship") in 2018…

| Jan-Krzysztof Duda (3250)  Martyn Kravtsiv (2990) | 1-0 | 32 | 2026 | [...] ## Early Life And Career (1998-2013)

After learning to play chess at the age of five, Duda’s first FIDE rating list came in October 2006, when he had an 1834 rating at age eight. Two years later, he played in the World Youth Championship and won first place in the under-10 division, earning the title of FIDE master. The result also moved him past the 2000-rating marker.

In 2010 he took a shot at the World Junior Championship for players under age 20 and held his own with a 50-percent score (+4 -4 =5). He also played in the youth under-12 event.

Duda began 2012 with his rating past the 2400 mark and then enjoyed a successful run in youth events, winning Poland’s under-18 and Europe’s under-14 events that year. As a result, he made IM.

## Grandmaster (2013-18) [...] In 2021, Duda outdid himself with a victory in the World Cup. He toppled Carlsen in tiebreaks in the semifinals before defeating GM Sergey Karjakin in the finals.
